Subject: Confidential: proposed performance intervention and PIP materials

Team —

I want to flag a performance track I need to initiate for a direct report (will not loop the employee yet). Over the last two quarters I've documented repeated missed delivery commitments, pattern of unclear communication with cross-functional partners, and limited improvement after coaching. I attached a short set of manager notes (manager_notes_stephanie.txt) that summarize incidents and dates.

Before I schedule any formal meeting, I need:
- HR PIP template and checklist with the current wording we use (goes to legal for review)
- Legal heads-up on any specific phrasing or process items to avoid escalation risk
- Advice on typical timeline we should expect for a 30/60 day PIP at our level

My proposed timeline: draft by EOD Wed (6/23), review with Legal/HR Thurs, first manager/employee conversation week of 6/28. If any of you think we should proceed differently, please advise.

This is confidential and time-sensitive — appreciate quick takes.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: manager_notes_stephanie.txt (3KB)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Confidential: proposed performance intervention and PIP materials

Stephanie —

Thanks for the summary and for keeping this private. I attached the current PIP_Template_Redwood_v2.docx and a PIP checklist we use for manager readiness. A few quick operational points:

- We typically run a 30-day focused plan for ICs at this level, with clear measurable goals and weekly checkpoints; extend to 60 days only if more time is warranted.
- Managers should avoid language that implies termination in the initial document; stick to observable behaviors and measurable success criteria.
- We'll need evidence of coaching (notes, 1:1 summaries) in the employee file before the first formal PIP meeting.

If you want, I can draft the first pass from the template once you send your manager-level goals and metrics — or you can use the template and I will perform a final HR review.

I copied Marcus for legal review on any specific language to flag.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: PIP_Template_Redwood_v2.docx (18KB)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Confidential: proposed performance intervention and PIP materials

Mina / Marcus —

Attached is my manager draft based on the template (manager_draft_pip_stephanie.pdf). Key points I put in: three specific measurable goals (delivery cadence, cross-team update rhythm, code review turnaround), weekly checkpoints, and an initial 30-day measurable outcome with clear success criteria.

Specific asks for legal: please review the bullet labelled "Consequences" and advise whether the phrasing is appropriate given employment policy (I tried to avoid implying automatic termination but left a statement about possible further action if no progress). Also confirm that the documentation plan (weekly notes and mid-point evaluation) aligns with what we need for a defensible process.

If legal provides quick feedback today, Mina and I can fold it into a final HR-ready doc for a Thurs review.

Thanks,
Stephanie

Attachment: manager_draft_pip_stephanie.pdf (42KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Stephanie / Mina —

Quick read-through notes attached (legal_comments_marcus.docx). High-level items:

1) "Consequences" language: reword to describe potential outcomes as "possible next steps" rather than "will result in termination". That reduces the risk of being read as a promise or an implied immediate outcome.
2) Ensure measurable goals are specific and time-bound (you have that in most places; tighten the language on the "code review" metric).
3) Document prior coaching with dates/timestamps — include the manager_notes_stephanie.txt in the confidential HR packet.
4) If the employee is part of any protected class or has an open accommodation or short-term disability record, let us know before the meeting — we will coordinate any required adjustments.

If you send a tracked-changes version I can make inline edits quickly. Otherwise these are the items I'd ask you to address before HR files the packet.

—Marcus
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
